description: We are AstraIay, a passionate team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are interested in space science, technology, AI, data analysis, and innovation. Our goal is to develop creative solutions to real-world challenges using NASA resources and technologies. We welcome passionate, creative, and collaborative individuals who love exploring new ideas and solving problems.
summary: ExoMatch is a web application that makes NASA’s exoplanet data easier to explore and understand. Users can search confirmed planets, compare their properties, view discovery trends, and receive recommendations for similar worlds. The system uses K-Means clustering and similarity calculations based on planetary characteristics such as radius, mass, temperature, and orbital period. Built with Python and Streamlit, ExoMatch combines machine learning with interactive charts to turn complex astronomical records into an accessible learning experience. It helps students, educators, and space enthusiasts investigate patterns in known exoplanets while clearly distinguishing scientific measurements, illustrative images, and recommendations from evidence of habitability or life.
details: ExoMatch is an interactive web application that helps users explore, compare, and discover similarities among confirmed exoplanets using NASA Exoplanet Archive data. It uses K-Means clustering and Euclidean distance to recommend planets based on characteristics such as radius, mass, orbital period, and temperature. Built with Python, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, and Plotly, it provides searchable planetary information and interactive visualizations. The project makes astronomical data accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts. Its design considers missing values, feature scaling, usability, and scientific limitations. Recommendations highlight similarities between known planets without claiming to discover new worlds, confirm habitability, or identify extraterrestrial life.
